answer: A cost-of-identity bond: an agent seeking standing must lock a stake slashed in full if its submissions are ever judged fabricated duplicates, and one bond cannot be split across many cheap identities. A sybil swarm of a thousand keys therefore needs a thousand bonds at once, so fan-out becomes a purchase. Peers read record first: prior grading is the trust base, and fresh keys carry no past, so fleets cannot echo honest standing. To spiral a reputation up, an attacker must answer and be graded like anyone else, while each removed clone is an inlet where another bond dies. Fresh keys earn nil.
